warning.SHELF_DEFLECTION: A {{spanMm}} mm shelf sags {{deflectionMm}} mm under {{loadKg}} kg, against {{limitMm}} mm allowed: it will show. Three ways out — go to {{thickerMm}} mm, shorten the span to {{maxSpanMm}} mm, or add an upright in the middle, which divides the sag by sixteen.
warning.NO_BACK_PANEL: Without a back panel the carcass racks over time.
warning.FRONT_GAP_OFF_DIVIDER: A front gap does not sit on its divider.
warning.COMPARTMENT_TOO_NARROW: A bay is too narrow for what it must hold.
warning.DRAWER_DOES_NOT_FIT: A drawer does not fit its bay: no parts are produced for it.
warning.DOOR_DOES_NOT_FIT: A door leaf does not fit its bay: no parts are produced for it.
warning.DOOR_LEAF_TOO_WIDE: A door leaf is wide: it will pull on its hinges and end up rubbing. Fit a pair.
warning.NO_SLIDE_FITS: No off-the-shelf slide fits {{usableDepthMm}} mm of usable depth: the drawer is left undrilled.
warning.COMPARTMENT_WIDTH_MISMATCH: The fixed widths add up to {{requestedMm}} mm for {{availableMm}} mm available.
warning.PULL_WITHOUT_FACADE: A handle in compartment {{compartment}} no longer has a facade.
warning.PULL_OFF_FACADE: A handle overhangs its {{facadeWidthMm}} × {{facadeHeightMm}} mm facade.
warning.SPACE_TOO_NARROW: The piece is {{furnitureMm}} mm wide for {{spaceMm}} mm available.
warning.SPACE_TOO_SHORT: The piece is {{furnitureMm}} mm tall including legs, for {{spaceMm}} mm of ceiling height.
warning.SPACE_TOO_SHALLOW: The piece is {{furnitureMm}} mm deep for {{spaceMm}} mm available.
warning.CANNOT_TILT_UP: It stands, but cannot be raised in place: assembled flat it needs {{tiltMm}} mm to tilt up, and the ceiling is at {{spaceMm}} mm. Assemble it upright, or outside the room.
warning.SKIRTING_HOLDS_OFF: The skirting board holds the piece {{gapMm}} mm off the wall: it will take {{totalDepthMm}} mm of floor. Notch the back, or allow for the gap.
warning.DOOR_SWING_CLEARANCE: The doors need {{clearanceMm}} mm in front of the piece to open.
warning.SHELF_DEFLECTION_NO_THICKNESS: A {{spanMm}} mm shelf sags {{deflectionMm}} mm under {{loadKg}} kg, against {{limitMm}} mm allowed: it will show. No catalogue thickness is enough — shorten the span to {{maxSpanMm}} mm, or add an upright in the middle, which divides the sag by sixteen.

assembly.carcass: Join the bottom to the sides, sides inside, flush with the edges.
assembly.top: Fit the top onto the sides, flush with the edges.
assembly.dividers: Set the dividers plumb between bottom and top.
assembly.shelves: Rest the shelves on their supports.
assembly.back: Slide the back into its groove, then check the carcass is square.
assembly.drawers: Build the drawer boxes: sides, front, back, then bottom.
assembly.drawer_faces: Fit the faces onto the boxes, with an even gap between them.
assembly.doors: Hang the doors last, then adjust the hinges: an even gap all the way round.

glossary.edge_banding: The thin strip glued onto the cut edge of a board. Without it you see the core — chipboard or plies — exactly where the piece is looked at and touched.
glossary.trim: The strip removed from each edge of a new board before cutting. Factory edges are neither straight nor square: cutting into them gives wrong parts.
glossary.kerf: The material the blade turns into sawdust, about 3 mm. Two 600 parts do not fit in 1200: the width of the cut is always missing.
glossary.shelf_support: The small, often metal support pushed into a 5 mm hole in the upright, on which the shelf rests. Four per shelf, and they can be moved.
glossary.hinge_plate: The half of the hinge screwed to the cabinet upright. The other half — the cup — sits in the door.
glossary.hinge_cup: The round part of the hinge, housed in a 35 mm hole bored in the door. That hole is what needs a Forstner bit.
glossary.dowel: A wooden pin glued into two facing holes. Invisible once assembled, but the two holes must line up to a tenth of a millimetre.
glossary.pilot_hole: The narrow hole drilled before driving a screw, in the part that receives it. It keeps the board from splitting and guides the screw straight.
glossary.clearance_hole: The wide hole drilled in the part the screw passes through. The screw must run freely: otherwise it pushes the parts apart instead of pulling them together.
glossary.grain: The direction of the fibres, visible on a wood decor. Two neighbouring parts whose grain runs differently show from three metres away.
glossary.yield: The share of the bought board that becomes parts. The rest is offcut. 70 % is common; below that, it is often worth revisiting the sizes.
glossary.forstner: A flat-bottomed bit that bores large, flat-bottomed holes. It is the only one that makes a clean hinge housing.
glossary.countersink: A tool that widens the mouth of a hole into a cone, so the screw head sits flush instead of holding the board apart.
glossary.slide: The rail a drawer runs on. They are sold in pairs and by length — you buy a pair of 400, not "some slides".
